climate.sub: Coastal humidity changes which fabric actually works, and it is the first thing we ask a Miami team about.
prose: Miami's problem is not only temperature — it is humidity that stays high after the sun goes down. Sweat evaporates more slowly when the surrounding air is already saturated, which is why a jersey that performs well in a dry climate can feel heavy here by the second quarter.

That pushes most Miami orders toward one of two answers. An open-weave mesh lets heat leave through the fabric, which works best where there is some air movement — an outdoor court, a hall with the doors open. A moisture-wicking knit moves sweat to the outer face of the fabric, which works better in still indoor air where there is no breeze for mesh to use.

Programs playing in older Miami-Dade gyms without full air conditioning usually end up in mesh. Programs in newer conditioned arenas do better with the wicking knit, because the building is already handling the heat and what remains is the sweat.
